stories.headline: Jensen Huang unveils Vera Rubin GPU at GTC, projects $1T in AI chip orders

key_facts.fact: At the GTC 2026 keynote on March 16, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang unveiled the Vera Rubin GPU platform, successor to Blackwell, built on TSMC 3nm with HBM4 memory delivering 3.0+ TB/s bandwidth and 50 petaFLOPS of FP4 inference per chip.
key_facts.excerpt: Jensen Huang just put Nvidia's Blackwell and Vera Rubin sales projections into the $1 trillion stratosphere.

key_facts.fact: Huang projected $1 trillion worth of orders for Nvidia's Blackwell and Vera Rubin chip generations combined, up from a previous $500 billion forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: Jensen Huang just put Nvidia's Blackwell and Vera Rubin sales projections into the $1 trillion stratosphere.

key_facts.fact: Vera Rubin delivers 5x inference performance improvement over Blackwell Ultra in FP4 workloads and a 10x reduction in inference token costs, requiring 4x fewer GPUs for Mixture-of-Experts training.
key_facts.excerpt: Vera Rubin delivers 5x inference performance improvement over Blackwell Ultra in FP4 workloads and a 10x reduction in inference token costs.

key_facts.fact: The VR200 NVL144 flagship rack configuration pairs 144 Vera Rubin GPUs with the new Vera CPU, and the platform includes 288 GB of HBM4 per GPU with 336 billion transistors.
key_facts.excerpt: 336 billion transistors. 288 GB of HBM4 per GPU. 22 TB/s memory bandwidth. 50 petaFLOPS of FP4 inference per chip.

key_facts.fact: Huang also teased the Feynman architecture for 2028, using TSMC A16 1.6nm process with silicon photonics for 10x inter-chip bandwidth improvement, and confirmed Vera Ultra for H2 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Feynman: 2028 launch, uses TSMC A16 1.6nm process, incorporates silicon photonics for 10x inter-chip bandwidth improvement.

key_facts.fact: The keynote drew over 30,000 attendees from 190+ countries at the SAP Center in San Jose, with Huang describing AI as 'essential infrastructure, like electricity.'
key_facts.excerpt: In front of 30,000 attendees from 190 countries, NVIDIA's CEO unveiled a sweeping vision that goes far beyond chips... AI is no longer a technology feature. It is essential infrastructure, like electricity.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches NemoClaw to add security and privacy controls to OpenClaw agents

key_facts.fact: At GTC 2026 on March 16, Nvidia announced NemoClaw, a security and privacy wrapper for the open-source OpenClaw agent platform, combining Nvidia's Nemotron models with a new OpenShell sandbox runtime.
key_facts.excerpt: NemoClaw, announced Monday at GTC 2026, installs Nvidia's Nemotron models and the newly released Nvidia OpenShell runtime onto the fast-growing open-source AI agent platform OpenClaw in a single command, adding privacy and security guardrails to autonomous AI agents.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang declared 'OpenClaw is the operating system for personal AI' and called it 'the fastest-growing open source project in history,' positioning NemoClaw as the enterprise-ready security layer.
key_facts.excerpt: 'OpenClaw opened the next frontier of AI to everyone and became the fastest-growing open source project in history,' Huang said. 'OpenClaw is the operating system for personal AI.'

key_facts.fact: OpenShell runs OpenClaw in a sandbox that prevents access to unnecessary files and limits network access, with developers able to customize policies via YAML configuration rules that are hot-swappable without restarting the agent.
key_facts.excerpt: The first is OpenShell, a tool that adds privacy and cybersecurity guardrails to OpenClaw. It does so by running OpenClaw in a sandbox that prevents it from accessing files not necessary to the tasks it performs. The tool also limits the agent's network access.

key_facts.fact: NemoClaw runs on GeForce RTX PCs, RTX PRO workstations, DGX Station and DGX Spark, enabling always-on autonomous agents locally without routing sensitive data through the cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: NemoClaw runs on any dedicated platform — including GeForce RTX PCs and laptops, RTX PRO workstations, DGX Station and DGX Spark — so teams can run always-on autonomous agents locally without routing sensitive data through the cloud.

key_facts.fact: Alongside NemoClaw, Nvidia announced Nemotron 3 Ultra, Nemotron 3 Omni, and Nemotron VoiceChat models to extend multimodal intelligence for specialized agentic AI workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: Nemotron 3 Ultra, Omni and VoiceChat aim to 'extend multimodal intelligence to help deliver specialized, agentic AI.'

key_facts.fact: The Nemotron model family includes Nemotron 3 Nano (30B/3B active), Nemotron 3 Super (~100B/10B active), and the upcoming Nemotron 3 Ultra (~500B/50B active, expected H1 2026), all designed for agentic AI workloads.

key_facts.excerpt: LangChain is also joining the Nemotron Coalition, NVIDIA's global initiative to advance frontier open AI models through shared expertise, data, and compute.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also confirmed Groq 3 LPUs for ultralow-latency inference as part of expanded AWS infrastructure, spanning the full Nvidia AI computing stack including Blackwell and Rubin GPU architectures.

stories.headline: Mistral AI releases Mistral Small 4, a 119B-parameter open MoE unifying reasoning and multimodal

key_facts.fact: Mistral AI released Mistral Small 4 on March 16, a 119B total parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 128 experts, 4 active per token, and only 6.5B active parameters — the first model to unify instruct, reasoning, multimodal, and agentic coding in a single deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral Small 4 is a Mixture of Experts model with 128 experts, 4 active per token. Total Parameters: 119B. Active Parameters: 6.5B per token.

key_facts.fact: The model supports 256K token context, Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), toggleable reasoning mode per request, native function calling, and multilingual support across 20+ languages.
key_facts.excerpt: Context Length: 256k tokens. Attention Mechanism: MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention). Reasoning Mode: Toggleable per-request (reasoning_effort='none' or reasoning_effort='high').

key_facts.fact: Mistral Small 4 achieves 40% reduction in end-to-end completion time and 3x more requests per second compared to Mistral Small 3, with GPQA Diamond score of 71.2 and MMLU-Pro of 78.0.
key_facts.excerpt: Latency-Optimized: 40% reduction in end-to-end completion time vs Mistral Small 3. Throughput-Optimized: 3x more requests per second vs Mistral Small 3. GPQA: 71.2 (Diamond tier). MMLU-Pro: 78.0.

key_facts.fact: Released under Apache 2.0 license with open weights, the model replaces four separate Mistral models (Mistral Small, Magistral, Pixtral, and Devstral) and runs on 2 GPUs via vLLM with NVFP4 quantization available.
key_facts.excerpt: License: Apache 2.0. Mistral Small 4 is its first model to combine the roles associated with Mistral Small for instruction following, Magistral for reasoning, Pixtral for multimodal understanding, and Devstral for agentic coding.

stories.headline: LangChain ships Deep Agents, open-source harness scoring 42.65% on Terminal Bench 2.0

key_facts.fact: LangChain released Deep Agents on March 15, an MIT-licensed open-source agent harness for long-horizon, multi-step tasks built on LangGraph, available via 'pip install deepagents'.
key_facts.excerpt: Available now via pip install deepagents; MIT licensed. LangChain shipped Deep Agents, an open-source agent harness for long-running, complex tasks.

key_facts.fact: The Deep Agents CLI scored ~42.65% on Terminal Bench 2.0 using Claude Sonnet 4.5, competitive with Claude Code at the same model tier, across two runs averaging 44.9% and 40.4%.
key_facts.excerpt: The Deep Agents CLI scored ~42.65% on Terminal Bench 2.0 using Claude Sonnet 4.5, on par with Claude Code at the same model tier.

key_facts.fact: The architecture includes four core pillars: task planning with a built-in write_todos tool, isolated subagents with separate context windows, persistent memory via a virtual filesystem backed by LangGraph's state store, and a detailed system prompt modeled on Claude Code's architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: It's built on LangGraph and includes planning, subagents, persistent memory, and a virtual filesystem.

key_facts.fact: Deep Agents is model-agnostic and supports pluggable backends for memory storage (S3, local disk, in-memory), but currently lacks OS-level sandboxing and operates with a 'trust the LLM' security model.
key_facts.excerpt: No OS-level sandbox (uses 'trust the LLM' model with tool-level boundaries). Persistent Memory: A virtual filesystem backed by LangGraph's state store offloads artifacts and intermediate files, keeping working context lean. Supports pluggable backends (S3, local disk, in-memory).

stories.headline: MiroMind's MiroThinker-H1 sets SOTA on BrowseComp and FrontierScience, beating GPT-5.4

key_facts.fact: On March 16, MiroMind released MiroThinker-1.7 and its flagship system MiroThinker-H1, achieving state-of-the-art on BrowseComp (88.2 vs Gemini-3.1-Pro 85.9, Claude-4.6-Opus 84.0, GPT-5.4 82.7), BrowseComp-ZH (84.4), and FrontierScience-Olympiad (79.0 vs GPT-5.2 77.1).
key_facts.excerpt: MiroThinker-H1 has achieved state-of-the-art results across the most demanding multi-step reasoning and deep research benchmarks in the field, surpassing frontier systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind.

key_facts.fact: The system introduces 'Effective Interaction Scaling' — improving the quality and reliability of every reasoning step rather than scaling model size or compute, using a novel dual-layer verification system at inference time.
key_facts.excerpt: MiroThinker introduces a paradigm-shifting approach called 'Effective Interaction Scaling' — improving the quality and reliability of every reasoning step, rather than blindly increasing the number of steps.

key_facts.fact: The Local Verifier audits intermediate decisions in real-time, reducing average interaction steps by ~82% while improving accuracy by +26.4 points on hard BrowseComp subsets; the Global Verifier reviews complete reasoning trajectories leveraging generation-verification asymmetry.
key_facts.excerpt: Local Verifier: Audits intermediate decisions in real-time, reducing average interaction steps by ~82% while improving accuracy by +26.4 points on hard BrowseComp subsets.

key_facts.fact: MiroThinker-1.7 achieved a Report Quality score of 76.5 on deep research, slightly exceeding OpenAI Deep Research (76.4), with the training pipeline combining agentic mid-training, supervised fine-tuning, DPO, and GRPO reinforcement learning.
key_facts.excerpt: MiroThinker-1.7 achieved Report Quality score of 76.5, slightly exceeding OpenAI Deep Research (76.4). Four integrated stages: Agentic Mid-Training, Supervised Fine-Tuning, Direct Preference Optimization, and Reinforcement Learning with GRPO.

stories.headline: Cuba's national power grid collapses amid US oil blockade, 10M without power

key_facts.fact: Cuba's national electric grid collapsed on March 16, leaving around 10 million people without power, as grid operator UNE confirmed while investigating the cause.
key_facts.excerpt: Cuba's national electric grid has collapsed, leaving around 10 million people without power amid a U.S.-imposed oil blockade that has crippled the island's already obsolete generation system.

key_facts.fact: Cuba has received only two small oil import vessels in 2026 — one from Mexico discharging fuel in January and one from Jamaica with cooking gas in February — after Trump cut off Venezuelan oil shipments and threatened tariffs on any country selling oil to Cuba.
key_facts.excerpt: Cuba has received only two small vessels carrying oil imports this year... The first tanker discharged fuel in January at the Havana port coming from Mexico. The second vessel, from Jamaica, discharged liquefied petroleum gas in February.

key_facts.fact: The blackouts sparked a rare violent protest in the communist-run country over the weekend. Cuba entered talks with the US on Friday to try to defuse the crisis.

stories.headline: GEN Pharma gets ethics approval for SUL-238 Phase II trial targeting Parkinson's disease

key_facts.fact: GEN Pharmaceuticals received approval on March 16 from the Netherlands' BEBO Foundation to proceed with a Phase II Proof of Concept trial of SUL-238 targeting mitochondrial dysfunction in Parkinson's patients.
key_facts.excerpt: GEN Pharmaceuticals announced today that it has received approval in the Netherlands from the BEBO Foundation for the Assessment of Ethics of Biomedical Research to proceed with Phase II Proof of Concept Trial for SUL-238 Targeting Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Patients with Parkinson's Disease.

key_facts.fact: The trial, called the SHEPHERD Study, is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study that will use Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (31P-MRS) to assess SUL-238's effects on high energy phosphates in early, untreated Parkinson's patients.
key_facts.excerpt: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center Study to Assess the effects of SUL-238 on High Energy Phosphates with Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (31P-MRS) in patients with Early, untreated Parkinson's Disease ('SHEPHERD' STUDY).

key_facts.fact: Patient enrollment is planned to start in April 2026 at a clinical site in Groningen, the Netherlands. GEN is Türkiye's leading specialty pharmaceutical company, traded as GENIL.IS.
key_facts.excerpt: GEN can now proceed to activate the clinical site in Groningen, the Netherlands. Patient enrollment is planned to start in April 2026.

sources.title: GEN Receives Ethical Approval to Launch Phase II Clinical Trial for SUL-238 Targeting Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Patients with Parkinson's Disease
